`describe` accepts a function or a class as its title and prints its name. A string that repeats the name is not updated when you rename the function, so the test output keeps showing a name that no longer exists.

The rule reports a `describe` title that is a string equal to a name the file imports. A title like `slugify.name` is reported too.

`--fix-suggestions` replaces the title with the name, unless the import is type-only. `--fix` does not, because the import may not be a function or a class.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { slugify } from "./slugify";

describe("slugify", () => {
  test("replaces spaces", () => {
    expect(slugify("a b")).toBe("a-b");
  });
});
```

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { describe } from "bun:test";
import { slugify } from "./slugify";

describe(slugify.name, () => {});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { slugify } from "./slugify";

describe(slugify, () => {
  test("replaces spaces", () => {
    expect(slugify("a b")).toBe("a-b");
  });
});

describe("slugify with options", () => {});
```
